His comments on 知人者智，自知者明 and 勝人者有力，自勝者強, the key verse’s lines, read: 知人者，智而已矣，未若自知者超智之上也 and 勝人者，有力而已矣，未若自勝者無物以損其力，用其智於人，未若用其智於己也。用其力於人，未若用其力於己也. That carries mere cleverness and force (而已矣), falling short (未若) of turning both upon oneself, and nothing diminishing the self-overcomer’s strength. The closing relative clause hangs the strength on the one who turns both upon himself, where Wang Bi hangs it on the self-overcomer; since that same person overcomes himself, this is not drift. Plain sense (paired sayings ending on longevity) is faithful to both units and does not repeat the verse. verse.js ok (Tao Te Ching 33, at [32]); entry-check ok. No attack landed.
